related_questions.question: Which COVID test is most accurate?

text_blocks.snippet: The PCR test is generally considered the most accurate COVID-19 test. It works by detecting the virus's genetic material, making it highly sensitive and specific. While antigen tests, including at-home tests, are more convenient and faster, they are not as sensitive as PCR tests, especially when someone has few or no symptoms.

related_questions.question: What is the difference between PCR and antigen test?

text_blocks.snippet: PCR and antigen tests are both used to detect infections, but they differ in their approach and sensitivity. PCR tests are highly sensitive and can detect even small amounts of viral genetic material, while antigen tests, also known as rapid tests, are faster and easier to perform but are generally less sensitive.

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: PCR tests amplify the viral genetic material in a sample, making it easier to detect even trace amounts.

list.title: Sensitivity:
list.snippet: Highly sensitive, meaning they can accurately detect the virus even in early stages of infection or when viral load is low.

list.title: Accuracy:
list.snippet: Considered the gold standard for diagnosing SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19) due to their high accuracy, approaching 100% according to UMass Chan Medical School.

list.title: Turnaround Time:
list.snippet: Can take anywhere from 12 hours to several days to produce results, due to the need for specialized equipment and laboratory processing.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: Generally more expensive than antigen tests, often costing $100 or more per test.

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: Antigen tests detect specific proteins (antigens) on the surface of the virus.

list.title: Sensitivity:
list.snippet: Less sensitive than PCR tests, meaning they may not detect the virus in early stages or when viral load is low.

list.title: Accuracy:
list.snippet: Faster and easier to perform, but may have a higher rate of false negatives.

list.title: Turnaround Time:
list.snippet: Results are typically available within minutes, making them useful for rapid screening.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: Generally less expensive than PCR tests.
If speed and cost are primary concerns, an antigen test may be suitable.
If high accuracy and early detection are crucial, a PCR test is generally preferred.
